rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls an earlier Israelite offense and ingratitude, addressing their descendants as the same people because of their shared identity.
rows.anchor: تذكير لجناية أخرى لأسلاف بني إسرائيل وكفرانهم لنعمة الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the wilderness they tired of unchanging manna and quail, remembered their former agricultural life in Egypt, and longed for familiar habits.
rows.anchor: حين سئموا من أكل المن والسلوى لكونهما غير مبدلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired manna and quail counted as one food because eaten together; alternatively, “one” means an unvaried diet even if it has several dishes.
rows.anchor: وهما اثنان لأنهم كانوا يأكلون أحدهما بالآخر فيصيران طعاما واحدا

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī notes that Arabic can use a dual form for a single thing, as in the wording about pearls and coral, which come only from salt water.
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī cites al-Baghawī’s note that Arabic can use a dual form for one thing, as in the phrase about pearls and coral, which come only from salt water.
rows.anchor: وفي "تفسير البغوي" : والعرب تعبر عن الواحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that they could not bear everyone being self-sufficient, since mutual aid would disappear; they were also early adopters of servants and slaves.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لن نصبر على الغنى فيكون جميعنا أغنياء فلا يقدر بعضنا على الاستعانة ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fūm means wheat here because lentils belong to the same food category.
rows.anchor: وهو الحنطة لأن ذكر العدس يدل على أنه المراد لأنه من جنسه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another lexical view reads fūm as garlic because garlic and onion are paired as related foods.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو الثوم لأن ذكر البصل يدل على أنه هو المراد فإنه من جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baql denotes edible greens such as mint, celery, and leek; qiththāʾ is a cucumber-like plant.
rows.anchor: والبقل ما تنبت الأرض من الخضر والمراد أصناف البقول التي تأكلها الناس كالنعناع والكرفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request asks Moses to supplicate for them; the connective “so” makes their inability to endure the diet the cause of the request.
rows.anchor: سله لأجلنا بدعائك إياه والفاء لسببية عدم الصبر للدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “bring forth for us,” the object is omitted, and the verb is jussive as the response to the command to supplicate.
rows.anchor: يظهر لنا ويوجد شيئا فالمفعول محذوف والجزم لجواب الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording figuratively assigns growth to the receptive earth in place of God, the true agent; “min” is partitive and “mā” is relative.
rows.anchor: إسناد مجازي بإقامة القابل وهو الأرض مقام الفاعل وهو الله تعالى ومن تبعيضية وما موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “min” in “from its greens” is explanatory and functions circumstantially with the pronoun.
rows.anchor: من بيانية واقعة موقع الحال من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiththāʾ is related to qathd and resembles cucumber.
rows.anchor: أخو القثد وهي شيء يشبه الخيار

rows.speaker: ابن التمجيد
rows.claim: Ibn al-Tamjīd prefers reading fūm as garlic over wheat because it is mentioned with onion and lentils, which are cooked with garlic and onion.
rows.anchor: ابن التمجيد في "حواشيه" وحمله على الثوم أوفق من الحنطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lentils are a familiar seed whose measure by volume matches its weight.
rows.anchor: حب معروف يستوي كيله ووزنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Onion is a familiar green used to flavor cooking pots.
rows.anchor: بقل معروف تطيب به القدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause beginning “He said” is a new sentence answering an implied question about what God or Moses replied.
rows.anchor: استئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke asks whether they are choosing the lower thing for themselves in exchange for what is better; “adnā” is lower in rank and worth.
rows.anchor: أي : أقرب منزلة وأدون قدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exchange preposition attaches to what is relinquished, and manna and quail are better for taste, ease, and other reasons than the requested produce.
rows.anchor: فإن الباء تصحب الزائل دون الآتي الحاصل وخيرية المن والسلوى في اللذاذة وسقوط المشقة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say wheat is inferior here only in comparative value; the verse does not prove they wanted to replace manna and quail altogether, since they may have wanted alternation.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الحنطة وإن كانت أعلى من المن والسلوى لكن خساستها ههنا بالنسبة إلى قيمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Descend” means leave the wilderness if they want these foods.
rows.anchor: انحدروا وانزلوا من التيه إن كنتم تريدون هذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miṣr means any town, not Pharaoh’s Egypt: the Israelites had been commanded to enter the Holy Land, so Egypt would not fit.
rows.anchor: وإذا وجب عليهم دخول تلك الأرض فكيف يجوز دخول مصر فرعون وهو الأظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miṣr can mean a great town; its name is linked to cutting off open space through building, and it can be used for a town or village. It is indefinite here, so it declines.
rows.anchor: والمصر البلد العظيم من مصر الشيء بمصره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identifies Miṣr as Pharaoh’s Egypt; its declension is explained by its medial still consonant, or by construing it as “country” rather than “city.”
rows.anchor: وقيل : أريد به مصر فرعون وإنما صرف لسكون وسطه كهند ودعد ونوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that they will have what they asked for explains the command to descend.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالهبوط أي : فإن لكم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhilla means humiliation and maskana means poverty; the poor are called miskīn because poverty stills them and impedes movement.
rows.anchor: يسمى الفقير مسكينا لأن الفقر أسكنه وأقعده عن الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humiliation and poverty surround and cling to them like a dome, becoming an inescapable covering.
rows.anchor: جعلتا محيطتين بهم إحاطة القبة بمن ضربت عليه وألصقتا بهم وجعلتا ضربة لازب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their humiliation and poverty are retribution for ingratitude; the image is like plastering clay onto a wall, and even wealthy Jews seem poor.
rows.anchor: عنهم مجازاة لهم على كفرانهم كما يضرب الطين على الحائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To “return bearing” God’s anger means they deserved and bound themselves to it; the Prophet’s wording “I acknowledge” illustrates the verb.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم "أبوء بنعمتك علي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s anger means His censure of them in this world and punishment in the next.
rows.anchor: وغضب الله تعالى ذمه إياهم في الدنيا وعقوبتهم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the humiliation, poverty, their bearing the anger, and the great wrath.
rows.anchor: ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والبوء والغضب العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs include the conspicuous miracles shown through Moses, whether familiar or unfamiliar.
rows.anchor: الباهرة التي هي المعجزات الساطعة الظاهرة على يدي موسى عليه السلام مما عاد أو لم يعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disbelief also involved rejecting the Qur’an and Muhammad, denying his description in the Torah, and rejecting Jesus and the Gospel.
rows.anchor: وكذبوا بالقرآن ومحمد عليه السلام وأنكروا صفته في التوراة وكفروا بعيسى والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb, Zechariah, and John are named among the prophets they killed; “without right” stresses that even they did not regard the killings as justified.
rows.anchor: كشعيب وزكريا ويحيى عليهم السلام وفائدة التقييد مع أن قتل الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allowing prophets to be killed honors them and raises their rank, as with believers killed in God’s path; it is not abandonment.
rows.anchor: قيل ذلك كرامة لهم وزيادة في منازلهم كمثل من يقتل في سبيل الله من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan say only prophets not commanded to fight were killed, while every prophet commanded to fight was granted victory.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن رضي الله عنهم لم يقتل قط من الأنبياء إلا من لم يؤمر بقتال وكل من أمر بقتال نصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account does not conflict with 40:51 or 37:171–172; alternatively, victory can mean victory through proof and disclosure of truth, which every prophet had.
rows.anchor: مع أنه يجوز أن يراد به النصرة بالحجة وبيان الحق وكل منهم بهذا المعنى منصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Israelites killed seventy prophets in one day.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم قتلوا في يوم واحد سبعين نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawī couplet links foolishness with killing prophets and alludes to people calling the messengers ill omens.
rows.anchor: اين كار وكيا لازم آمد يقتلون الأنبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persistent disobedience and transgression led to the previously described disbelief and prophet-killing.
rows.anchor: يتجاوزون أمري ويرتكبون محارمي أي : جر بهم العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated minor sins lead to major sins, just as persistence in small acts of obedience leads toward greater acts.
rows.anchor: فإن صغار الذنوب إذا دووم عليها أدت إلى كبارها كما أن مداومة صغار الطاعات مؤدية إلى تحري كبارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heedlessness sickens the heart and prevents it from tasting faith; as fever makes sugar taste bitter, heedlessness is lethal poison to hearts.
rows.anchor: وسقم القلب بالغفلة عن الله تعالى منعهم عن إدراك لذاذة الإيمان وحلاوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers’ recoil from disobeying God resembles one’s recoil from poisoned food.
rows.anchor: فنفرة قلوب المؤمنين عن مخالفة الله نفرتك عن الطعام المسموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the servant has a will, but God’s will is better; “descend” means leaving surrender and divine governance for self-directed choice.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنمرادا وللعبد مرادا وما أراد الله خير فقوله : اهبطوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing and planning for oneself alongside God’s governance brings humiliation and poverty.
rows.anchor: إلى أرض التدبير والاختيار منكم لأنفسكم موصوفين بالذلة والمسكنة لاختياركم مع الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This community would not have spoken like Israel because of its brighter lights and penetrating spiritual insight; it is the balanced community of 2:143.
rows.anchor: لما قالت مقال بني إسرائيل لشفوف أنوارهم ونفوذ أسرارهم

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The inward analogy says Israel could not endure one heavenly food because of low nature, just as the lower human self cannot be content with one spiritual nourishment from God.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet says he is unlike others because he spends the night with his Lord, who feeds and gives him drink, modeling the soul’s endurance of spiritual nourishment.
rows.anchor: كما كان يصبر نفس النبي عليه السلام ويقول

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The lower self asks its heart, figured as Moses, for bodily produce: animal desires and physical pleasures; the answer is to exchange the perishing for the enduring.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد كان ينزل عليهم من السماء

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The inward Egypt is the lower body, reached by descending from the high stations of the spirit; its base demands bring beast-like degradation.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد كان ينزل

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Inward disbelief means denying unseen inspirations and spiritual unveilings; killing prophets means nullifying divinely opened reports of the unseen and denying their secrets.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد كان ينزل

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: These losses result from disobedience and breaking the covenant of striving in worship; transgression is seeking something other than God.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : كما أن بني إسرائيل لم يصبروا على طعام واحد كان ينزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse permits eating wholesome and pleasurable foods; the Prophet liked sweets and honey and drank cool, sweet water, while lentils and oil are foods of the righteous.
rows.anchor: ثم إن في الآية الكريمة دليلا على جواز أكل الطيبات والمطاعم المستلذات

rows.speaker: التتارخانية
rows.claim: If prayer begins sincerely and ostentation enters later, it follows the original intention; one who prays or beautifies prayer only before people earns the basic prayer’s reward, not its excellence.
rows.anchor: في "التتارخانية" لو افتتح للصلاة خالصاتعالى

rows.speaker: بعض الحكماء
rows.claim: A sage compares ostentatious worship to carrying a bag of pebbles to market: it earns praise from people but no real benefit.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء : مثل من يعمل الطاعة للرياء والسمعة

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A report urges people to purify their deeds for God, who accepts only what is sincerely for Him, and warns against claiming a deed is for God and kin when it is not.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "أخلصوا أعمالكمتعالى فإن الله لا يقبل إلا ما خلص له ولا تقولوا

rows.speaker: أحاديث المشارق
rows.claim: A report curses those who curse their parents and those who sacrifice to other than God.
rows.anchor: أحاديث المشارق "لعن الله من لعن والديه ولعن الله من ذبح لغير الله"

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawī explains sacrifice to other than God as slaughter done in the name of another, such as an idol or Moses.
rows.anchor: قال النووي المراد الذبح باسم غير الله كمن ذبح للصنم أو لموسى

rows.speaker: إبراهيم المراودي
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Marwādhī says Bukhara jurists deemed slaughtering for a ruler’s arrival, as a devotional approach to him, forbidden because it was offered to someone besides God.
rows.anchor: ذكر الشيخ إبراهيم المراودي : إن ما يذبح عند استقبال السلطان تقربا إليه

rows.speaker: الرافعي
rows.claim: Al-Rāfiʿī rejects that ruling: the slaughter celebrates the ruler’s arrival, like an ʿaqīqa for a newborn, so it is not forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقال الرافعي : هذا غير محرم لأنهم إنما يذبحونه استبشارا بقدومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adopts al-Rāfiʿī’s charitable reading of Muslims’ actions to protect them from charges of unbelief or wasted deeds; a monotheist seeks God’s approval through available acts of worship.
rows.anchor: وعليه تحمل أفعال المسلمين صيانة لهم عن الكفر وضياع الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “foolish” are people of weak understanding, especially unbelievers among hypocrites, Jews, and polytheists who object to the qibla change; they are foolish for turning from Abraham’s religion.
rows.anchor: الذين ضعفت عقولهم حال كونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The advance warning prepares believers, reducing the shock of the expected objection and supplying an answer before the need arises; preparation is better before an opponent’s attack.
rows.anchor: وفائدة تقديم الإخبار به قبل وقوعه ليوطئوا عليه أنفسهم فلا يضطربوا عند وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “what turned them” is an emphatic interrogative; the wording distinguishes turning away from something from turning someone toward another thing.
rows.anchor: ما استفهامية إنكارية مرفوعة المحل على الابتداء ووليهم خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibla first meant a person’s facing direction, then in religious usage the direction faced in prayer; it is named from facing it, and here means Jerusalem, replaced by the Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: والقبلة في الأصل الحالة التي عليها الإنسان من الاستقبال فنقلت في عرف الشرع في الجهة التي يستقبلها الإنسان للصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for about seventeen months after arriving in Medina to draw the Jews’ hearts, after which the Kaʿba became the Muslims’ qibla until the end of time.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي عليه السلام صلى إلى نحو بيت المقدس بعد مقدمه المدينة نحوا من سبعة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is that east and west, indeed all places, belong to God; no direction has an inherent claim to be qibla, and it becomes one only by God’s command.
rows.anchor: الأمكنة كلها والنواحي بأسرهاتعالى ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can command facing any direction at any time through His sovereignty and will, and the creature should obey without seeking extra qualities in the commanded act.
rows.anchor: فله أن يأمر في كل وقت بالتوجه إلى جهة من تلك الجهات على حسب ألوهيته واستيلائه ونفاذ قدرته ومشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s rulings and acts are not driven by causes or purposes; the command calls for compliance, since He is not answerable for what He does.
rows.anchor: لا تجري العلل والأغراض الداعية له تعالى إلى الأمر لأن أحكام الله تعالى وأفعاله ليست معللة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews chose the west from their own desire because they thought Moses had been on the western side, while Christians chose the east because Mary withdrew eastward.
rows.anchor: واليهود إنما استقبلوا جهة المغرب واتخذوها قبلة اتباعا لهوى أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers faced the Kaʿba in obedience rather than by their own ranking of directions, although it is Abraham’s qibla and Muhammad’s birthplace.
rows.anchor: والمؤمنون استقبلوا الكعبة طاعةتعالى وامتثالا لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is facing Jerusalem at one time and the Kaʿba at another; its straightness lies in its wisdom and benefit.
rows.anchor: وهو التوجه إلى بيت المقدس تارة والكعبة أخرى ووجه استقامته كونه مشتملا على الحكمة والمصلحة

rows.speaker: بعض أرباب الحقيقة
rows.claim: Some spiritual masters call the opponents foolish because their minds are veiled from Islam’s truth; sound reason and recognition of comprehensive divine unity would have ended their objection to the change.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أرباب الحقيقة : سمى الطاغين من اليهود والمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāmī’s couplet portrays the world as a mirror of the Beloved’s beauty and invites the viewer to see His face in every atom.
rows.anchor: جهان مرآت حسن شاهد ماست فشاهد وجهه في كل ذرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Likewise” points back to the preceding idea: God made the community guided to the straight path.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى مفهوم الآية المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Middle community” means the best community, since the middle is protected while the edges are more quickly exposed to flaws.
rows.anchor: خيارا لأن الأوساط محمية محوطة والأطراف يتسارع إليها الخلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community will testify on Judgment Day that the messengers delivered their messages, and Muhammad will testify over the community.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة أن الرسل قد بلغتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although testimony benefiting someone is usually expressed with “for,” the Prophet is “over” the community because shahīd includes the sense of watchful observer, whose praise rests on knowledge of their conduct.
rows.anchor: هذا مبني على تضمين الشهيد معنى الرقيب والمطلع فعدى تعديته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s testimony over the community singles them out for his commendation and does not conflict with his testimony for the prophets or against deniers of their delivery.
rows.anchor: لاختصاصهم بشهادته صلى الله عليه وسلم على سبيل التزكية والتعديل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first object of “make” is the qibla and the second is the relative clause, understood with an omitted noun; the direction was the Kaʿba in Mecca, Jerusalem after migration, then the Kaʿba again.
rows.anchor: أي : لجهة التي كنت عليها وهي الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test was to make evident who follows the Messenger in the commanded direction and who turns back, an image for abandoning true religion for falsehood.
rows.anchor: والانقلاب على العقبين مستعار للارتداد والرجوع عن الدين الحق إلى الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that We may know” means making God’s eternal knowledge manifest in events, distinguishing steadfast believers from weak, wavering people; it does not imply that God learned something new.
rows.anchor: ليظهر علمنا على مظاهر الرسول والمؤمنين ويتميز عندهم الثابت على الإسلام الصادق فيه

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qāshānī chooses the manifestation reading and rejects other interpretations; one near alternative makes the purpose that the Messenger and believers know, whose knowledge is attributed to God because they are His close ones.
rows.anchor: هذا هو المعنى الذي اختاره القاشاني في تأويلاته وزيف ما عداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “know” can mean recognize, which does not require a second object; although God is not called “knower” in the usual sense of knowledge preceded by ignorance, it may mean unqualified apprehension.
rows.anchor: والعلم في قوله لنعلم بمعنى المعرفة أي : لنعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “from the one who turns back” is circumstantial with the subject of “follows,” marking the distinction between the two groups.
rows.anchor: وقوله ممن ينقلب حال من فاعل يتبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changed qibla was difficult for people accustomed to the former direction, because people find it hard to leave a familiar habit.
rows.anchor: شاقة ثقيلة على من يألف التوجه إلى القبلة المنسوخة فإن الإنسان ألوف لما يتعوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “though it was difficult,” in is the lightened form of inna with an omitted noun, and the lām distinguishes it; 17:108 supplies a grammatical parallel.
rows.anchor: وإن هي المخففة من المثقلة واسمها محذوف وهو القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those God guided understand that legal rulings contain wisdom even when its particular rationale is unknown; the fortunate obey their wise Lord and the wretched disobey their all-knowing Lord.
rows.anchor: هداهم إلى حكمة الإحكام وأرشدهم وعرفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will not waste the community’s faith, meaning their steadfast affirmation of everything the Prophet brought without doubt.
rows.anchor: ثباتكم على التصديق بجميع ما جاء به النبي عليه السلام من غير أن ترتابوا في شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is immensely compassionate in moving them by mercy to the new direction, which is better for them, and merciful in forgiving through faith and providing sustenance.
rows.anchor: ذو مرحمة عظيمة لهم حيث نقلهم برحمته من ذلك إلى هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿdī’s couplet says the merciful draw near to the distressed and answer those who pray.
rows.anchor: فروماند كانرا برحمت قريب تضرع كنانرا بدعوت مجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report tells of a murderous, unjust ruler in David’s time who, abandoned by his idols, called on God and was rescued by Gabriel; God says He answered the one who called, or there would be no difference between Him and the idols.
rows.anchor: روي أنه أخذ بعض أمراء الكفار وكان جائرا قاتلا في زمن داود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some apostatized when the qibla changed because they were attached to what is other than God and had not surrendered to divine decree; they were swept away by spiritual murk.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن جماعة قد ارتدوا عن الإسلام عند تحويل القبلة لتعلقهم بما سوى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritually felicitous are attached neither to Jerusalem nor the Kaʿba, but to their Creator; they efface their own will and receive God’s will with joy and purity.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين سعدوا سعادة أزلية فلم يتعلقوا في الحقيقة بيت المقدس ولا بالكعبة بل الرب الخالق لهما

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: Ṣāʾib’s Persian couplet warns that the seeker of annihilation should not be bound by attachments.
rows.anchor: قال الصائب : مهياي فنارا ازعلايق نيست روايى

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم الجنيد البغدادي
rows.claim: Junayd rebukes people who claim to love him but flee when tested, saying actions belie their words and a true lover is captive to what comes from the beloved.
rows.anchor: ذكر أن أبا القاسم الجنيد البغدادي لما رأوه في وادي الوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets’ and saints’ most severe trials are sweeter than sweets to lovers, who wear surrender and patience and plunge into unveilings and witnessed realities.
rows.anchor: فلذلك قد عد أشد البلاء عند الأنبياء والأولياء ألذ من الحلوى فاكتسبوا حلل التسليم والاصطبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By keeping heart and tongue occupied with divine unity and remembrance, and treating attention to anything else as an obstacle, the lovers reach the utmost annihilation and subsistence.
rows.anchor: واشتغلوا مع الجنان واللسان بالتوحيد وذكر الملك المنان حتى عدوا الالتفات إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a spiritual admonition, God tells Moses to wait for vision until made enduring and reminds him that he tended Shuʿayb’s sheep for ten years before seeking vision after only forty days of worship.
rows.anchor: ولما قال موسى عليه السلام : رب أرني أنظر إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mountain tells Moses that God raised it by grace after Moses once tended sheep there with a cap and staff.
rows.anchor: فقال الجبل : يا موسى كنت ترعى الغنم في وعلى رأسك قلنسوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing prayer asks for steadfastness on God’s path, following the Messenger, and guidance toward the Kaʿba of the divine essence and the vision of God.
rows.anchor: اللهم اجعلنا على صراطك المستقيم واتباع رسولك الكريم واهدنا التوجه إلى كعبة ذاتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should seek help through patience and prayer in everything they do and leave undone; patience includes enduring hardship, resisting sin, and resisting the ego’s demands.
rows.anchor: في كل ما تأتون وما تذرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the greatest worship, the believer’s ascent, and the object of the Lord’s reward.
rows.anchor: التي هي أم العبادات ومعراج المؤمنين ومثاب رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when an affair troubled the Prophet, he turned to prayer and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: روي أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience and prayer are singled out because patience is the hardest inward bodily practice and prayer the hardest outward one, gathering many acts and disciplines that require divine aid.
rows.anchor: لأن الصبر أشد الأعمال الباطنة على البدن والصلاة أشد الأعمال الظاهرة عليها لأنها مجمع أنواع الطاعات

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn says abstention precedes positive action, like purification before adornment and negation before affirmation in the testimony of faith; prayer is listed because every believer can practice patience against sin and pray.
rows.anchor: قال عصام الدين قدم الترك على الفعل لأن التخلية قبل التحلية ولهذا قدم النفي في كلمة التوحيد

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn says zakat and pilgrimage are omitted because they apply only to people with sufficient wealth or ability, while fasting is itself restraint from food, drink, and other acts.
rows.anchor: وأما الزكاة فمختصة بأصحاب النصاب وأما الحج فبأصحاب الاستطاعة والصوم صبر عن معصية الأكل والشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being “with” the patient means lasting guardianship that brings aid and answered prayer; the preposition suits them because they directly practice patience.
rows.anchor: بالنصرة وإجابة الدعوة فمعنى المعية الولاية الدائمة المستتبعة لهما

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn explains God’s presence with the patient by their continued remembrance; the impatient are distracted by worldly worries even if they owned the whole world.
rows.anchor: إن الله مع الصابرين لأن الصابرين لا يذهلون عن ذكره بخلاف المجتنبين عن الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is higher than patience because patience may occur without prayer, while prayer necessarily includes patience; therefore God’s presence with the patient implies, a fortiori, His presence with those who pray.
rows.anchor: إذ قد ينفك الصبر عن الصلاة ولا تنفك الصلاة عن الصبر ذكر ههنا الصابرين
